performance.what_the_data_shows:
What the data shows
- Mobile performance is the primary constraint: average FCP 4379.6 ms, average LCP 7407.2 ms, average Speed Index 7996.7 ms, and average Total Blocking Time (TBT) 315.3 ms.
- Desktop is materially better but still not consistently fast on LCP: average FCP 1315.6 ms, average LCP 4577.8 ms, average Speed Index 3964.7 ms, and average TBT 65.4 ms.
- Page weight is high and dominated by images: average total transfer ~5.14 MB (mobile) / ~5.02 MB (desktop) with ~4.38 MB of that being images on both.
- Server response time is moderate (site origin ~329.6 ms mobile and ~371.6 ms desktop averages), suggesting the bigger bottleneck is payload/rendering rather than pure backend latency.
- Main-thread work is significantly heavier on mobile (avg ~2821 ms) than desktop (avg ~867 ms), with most time landing in the generic "Other" bucket, then style/layout and script evaluation.
performance.key_strengths:
Key strengths
- No HTTP errors observed in the sampled runs: average non-200 requests are 0 on both mobile and desktop.
- Third-party transfer is relatively contained compared to total weight (avg ~220.5 KB mobile; ~99.8 KB desktop), indicating the heaviest costs are first-party assets (notably images).
- Desktop responsiveness is generally good: average TBT 65.4 ms suggests limited long tasks on desktop relative to mobile.
- Server latency is not extreme and is consistent across pages (site origin response times cluster roughly ~300-625 ms in the per-URL data).
performance.primary_weaknesses:
Primary weaknesses
- LCP is consistently high, especially on mobile (avg 7407.2 ms), pointing to slow loading/rendering of the largest above-the-fold content (very likely large hero/gallery images given image transfer dominance).
- Excessive image transfer: site averages show ~4.38 MB images out of ~5.14 MB total on mobile; some pages are far higher (homepage ~17.6 MB images).
- High request count and task count on key pages: mobile averages are 30 requests and 4885 tasks, but the homepage spikes to 76 requests and 13,548 tasks, correlating with higher TBT and worse LCP.
- Main-thread pressure on mobile (avg ~2821 ms; homepage ~4323 ms) plus elevated mobile TBT (avg 315 ms; homepage 541 ms) indicates too much work during critical load (script evaluation + style/layout + other work).
performance.high_level_roadmap:
High level roadmap
- Phase 1 (highest impact, low-to-medium effort): Reduce above-the-fold image cost on the homepage and other image-heavy pages
- - Reduce the transfer size and/or count of the top transferred images (e.g., the ~0.5-1.0 MB WebP images on the homepage) and prioritize only the truly critical image(s) for initial render.
- - Target the pages with the largest image transfer and request counts first (homepage, then portfolio/about).
- Phase 2 (high impact, medium effort): Reduce mobile main-thread and blocking time
- - Focus on reducing TBT on the worst pages (homepage, portfolio, services) by reducing work that contributes to script evaluation and style/layout time during load.
- - Aim to bring mobile TBT down from ~315 ms average and reduce main-thread work closer to the lower pages (e.g., contact).
- Phase 3 (medium impact, medium effort): Reduce overall page complexity and network overhead where feasible
- - Reduce request counts on the heaviest pages (homepage at 76 requests is a major outlier vs other pages at 14-23).
- - Continue monitoring server response times (site origin ~330-370 ms averages) and keep them stable as payload reductions roll out.

seo.what_the_data_shows:
What the data shows
- Overall Lighthouse SEO scores are strong: average score 0.92 on both mobile and desktop across 5 URLs.
- Most audits pass consistently across all URLs: meta description, document title, link text, image alt, robots.txt, hreflang, crawlable anchors, HTTP status, and crawlability all show pass states broadly.
- The primary recurring failure is canonical: site-wide summary shows canonical failing on 4 of 5 URLs (80% fail rate) on both mobile and desktop.
- Several audits are "not applicable" across the set (indexing, structured data, tap targets, viewport, plugins, charset) and therefore are not currently contributing to failures in this dataset.
seo.key_strengths:
Key strengths
- Strong baseline SEO hygiene across the site set (titles, meta descriptions, alt text, and link text all pass for all sampled URLs).
- Crawl accessibility is good: robots.txt present, pages are crawlable, and all sampled URLs return HTTP 200.
- International targeting audit (hreflang) passes on all sampled URLs, indicating consistent configuration in the tested pages.
seo.primary_weaknesses:
Primary weaknesses
- Missing or invalid canonical on most pages (4/5 URLs fail). This can cause duplicate-content ambiguity, dilute ranking signals, and create indexation uncertainty for similar/parameterized versions of pages.
- Canonical is the top failed audit and the only consistent failure in the dataset, making it the clearest single SEO remediation target.
seo.high_level_roadmap:
High level roadmap
- Phase 1 (highest impact, low effort): Fix canonical across all failing URLs
- - Ensure each page declares a single, correct, fully-qualified canonical URL that matches the preferred indexable version.
- - Validate that canonicals are consistent between mobile and desktop and do not conflict with redirects or alternate URL forms.
- Phase 2 (quality control, low effort): Add automated checks to prevent regression
- - Add a build/deploy verification step to confirm canonical is present and correct on every indexable page.
- - Re-run Lighthouse across key templates (homepage, portfolio, content pages) after changes to confirm canonical failures drop to 0.

prioritisation_method: Prioritised by (1) breadth of impact across URLs and devices, (2) magnitude of user-visible impact indicated by the metrics (LCP, Speed Index, TBT, transfer size, request/task counts), and (3) implementation effort inferred from whether the issue is primarily content/config (low effort) versus systemic/template/runtime behavior (medium/high effort).

key_findings.issue: Homepage page weight and image transfer are extreme, driving poor LCP and high mobile blocking time
key_findings.impact: Improves core loading experience on the most important entry page; expected gains in mobile LCP, Speed Index, and responsiveness by reducing the primary bottleneck (image payload and associated work).
key_findings.explanation: The homepage transfers ~18.4 MB total with ~17.6 MB images and 76 requests on both mobile and desktop, with mobile LCP 9710.0 ms and TBT 541.0 ms. This is far above site averages and is the single largest performance outlier.

key_findings.impact: Reduces duplicate-content ambiguity and consolidates ranking signals; likely improves indexation consistency and SEO resilience across the site.
key_findings.explanation: The SEO dataset shows canonical failing on 80% of sampled URLs on both mobile and desktop (4 failures out of 5 URLs). Other SEO audits largely pass, making canonical the clear highest-leverage fix.

key_findings.issue: Mobile LCP is consistently high across the site set
key_findings.impact: Faster perceived load and improved user engagement on mobile; addresses a key user-facing metric across all tested pages.
key_findings.explanation: Mobile average LCP is 7407.2 ms with similarly high mobile FCP (~4379.6 ms) and Speed Index (~7996.7 ms). Image transfer averages are high (~4.38 MB) and correlate strongly with LCP outcomes.

key_findings.issue: Mobile main-thread work and Total Blocking Time are elevated, especially on key pages
key_findings.impact: Improves interactivity and reduces input delay on mobile, particularly on the homepage and portfolio/services pages where blocking is highest.
key_findings.explanation: Mobile average TBT is 315.3 ms (vs 65.4 ms desktop). Pages like the homepage (541 ms) and portfolio (451 ms) are notably higher and also show higher main-thread work.

key_findings.issue: Request count variability suggests inconsistent payload discipline across templates
key_findings.impact: Reduces network overhead and improves reliability on mobile connections; helps stabilize Speed Index and overall load consistency.
key_findings.explanation: Site averages are ~30 requests, but the homepage is 76 requests while other pages range from 14-23 requests. Reducing outliers will improve consistency and reduce critical-path congestion.
